skill.name: picocom
skill.description: Use picocom and the included serial helper to connect to authorized IoT UART consoles, capture logs, and run serial security assessment workflows.
skill.summary: Connect to authorized IoT serial consoles with picocom and structured logging.
skill.author: BrownFineSecurity

security_audit.summary: The helper has legitimate serial-console functionality, but the skill also contains extensive offensive workflows for root shell bypass, persistence, credential discovery, firmware extraction, and network reconnaissance. Many Markdown and serial-device matches are false positives, but the confirmed findings include critical backdoor and password-file guidance. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Remove examples that add SSH keys, root-equivalent users, reverse shells, or startup backdoors. Replace them with defensive checks and cleanup guidance.

remediation.issue: Authentication bypass and shell escape walkthroughs
remediation.suggestion: Limit bootloader and restricted-shell content to authorized detection, reporting, and remediation. Avoid step-by-step bypass commands in marketplace content.
Remove commands that search for passwords, API keys, private keys, shadow files, and web secrets. Focus on reporting exposure without collecting secrets.
Replace firmware dumping and network transfer steps with lawful backup prerequisites, consent checks, and non-exfiltrating validation guidance.
Avoid shell=True for trigger scripts, require explicit confirmation, and support allowlisted command arrays instead of arbitrary shell strings.

remediation.issue: Sensitive logs default to temporary paths
remediation.suggestion: Default logs to a user-protected directory, set restrictive permissions, and add redaction guidance for passwords, tokens, and device identifiers.

content.user_title: Assess IoT UART Consoles with Picocom
content.value_statement: IoT UART testing is hard to observe and document reliably. This skill provides picocom workflows, serial logging, and helper commands for authorized device assessments.
actual_capabilities: Connects to USB serial adapters and UART consoles with picocom.
Runs single, batch, interactive, and passive monitor sessions through a Python helper.
Captures serial input and output to log files for review.
Detects common shell, U-Boot, and AT command prompts.
Guides authorized enumeration of embedded device firmware and services.
Supports triggered monitoring to compare baseline and event-driven UART output.
limitations: Requires local hardware access to the target device and serial adapter.
Requires picocom and Python pyserial on the operator machine.
The offensive examples require strict authorization and may be unsafe on production devices.
Serial logs can contain secrets and must be stored securely.

use_cases.title: Document a UART Assessment
use_cases.description: Capture a repeatable serial session while identifying prompts, firmware details, and exposed services on an authorized device.

use_cases.title: Monitor Boot Diagnostics
use_cases.description: Record boot logs and compare baseline output against triggered hardware or network events.

use_cases.title: Review Device Exposure
use_cases.description: Summarize console access, default credentials, service exposure, and logging evidence for a device security report.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Logged Session
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for an authorized device.
prompt_templates.prompt: Connect to my authorized UART device with the default USB serial adapter. Log the session, identify the prompt, and summarize safe next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Boot Output
prompt_templates.prompt: Monitor the serial console during a reboot. Capture boot messages, note timing, and highlight errors or exposed configuration values.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Triggered Logs
prompt_templates.prompt: Run passive UART monitoring, capture a baseline, trigger my approved test action, and compare output before and after the event.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Full Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an authorized UART assessment plan for this embedded device. Include logging, prompt discovery, safe enumeration, evidence handling, and cleanup steps.

output_examples.input: Connect to an authorized device and identify the console state.
output_examples.output: The session log shows a responsive shell prompt. The summary lists baud rate, prompt type, user context, and recommended evidence to collect next.

output_examples.input: Capture boot messages and summarize security-relevant observations.
output: Boot output was captured with timestamps.
The device exposed firmware version and network initialization details.
The report recommends protecting logs because they may contain identifiers or secrets.

output_examples.input: Compare UART output before and after an approved network trigger.
output_examples.output: The result separates baseline, trigger, and post-trigger output, then summarizes new messages and their timing.

best_practices: Use this skill only on devices you own or have explicit written permission to test.
Store serial logs in a protected directory and redact secrets before sharing reports.
Prefer read-only observation before making any device changes.
anti_patterns: Do not use persistence, shell escape, or credential discovery steps outside an approved test scope.
Do not store sensitive UART logs in shared temporary directories.
Do not run trigger scripts or device commands that you have not reviewed.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps connect to authorized IoT serial consoles, capture logs, and organize UART security testing workflows.

faq.question: Does it require hardware access?
faq.answer: Yes. You need a target device, a compatible serial adapter, and permission to test the device.

faq.question: Can it run interactive sessions?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper supports single commands, scripts, interactive mode, passive monitoring, and AT command mode.

faq.question: Are the included offensive examples safe?
faq.answer: They are only appropriate for authorized security testing. Several examples can modify devices or expose sensitive data.

faq.question: How should logs be handled?
faq.answer: Treat logs as sensitive. They can include passwords, keys, network details, and device identifiers.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
